results.title: Automated and distributed statistical analysis of economic agent-based models - ScienceDirect
results.content: By leveraging statistical model checking (SMC) (Agha, Palmskog, 2018, Legay, Lukina, Traonouez, Yang, Smolka, Grosu, 2019), a successful simulation-based verification approach from computer science, and MultiVeStA  (Gilmore, Reijsbergen, Vandin, 2017, Sebastio, Vandin, 2013), an SMC tool-box that can be integrated with existing simulators to perform automated and distributed statistical analysis, we aim to deliver a set of techniques and algorithms which: (i) is easy-to-use by the modeller, (ii) improves reproducibility of the results, (iii) distributes simulations across the cores of a machine or across computer networks, (iv) automatically chooses a sufficient number of simulations and simulation steps to reach a user-specified statistical confidence, and (v) automatically runs a variety of statistical tests that are often overlooked by practitioners. The method proposed by Guerini and Moneta (2017) for macro ABMs requires the model to be in a steady state and to remove the transient period from the analysis; calibration approaches based on simulated moments (Franke, Westerhoff, 2012, Grazzini, Richiardi, 2015, Winker, Gilli, Jeleskovic, 2007), as well as recent Bayesian techniques (see, e.g., Grazzini et al., 2017), apply to ergodic models.4 Further, our transient analysis can be employed to evaluate probabilities of observing certain patterns, which would support the use of validation metrics recently fproposed in the literature (see, e.g., Barde, 2016, Lamperti, 2018, Lamperti, 2018).
